audit.tech_stack: Go 1.26, Bubble Tea TUI, PagerDuty/OCM/Backplane APIs, AI providers

findings.title: Backplane client interpolates clusterID into URL path without encoding
findings.issue: clusterID sourced from PagerDuty alert custom_details is interpolated directly into the URL path via fmt.Sprintf without url.PathEscape(). A crafted cluster ID containing path traversal sequences could redirect the request to an unintended API path on the same server.
findings.impact: Bearer token sent to unintended path on backplane server. Requires compromised alerting pipeline. Same-origin path manipulation only.
findings.failure_scenario: Attacker injects cluster_id='../../admin/endpoint' into a PagerDuty alert; the backplane bearer token is sent to an unintended API path.

remediation.fix: Add url.PathEscape(clusterID) and url.PathEscape(reportID) in ListReports and GetReport
remediation.prevent: Add cluster ID format validation similar to OCM's clusterIDPattern

findings.title: OpenAI-compat provider sends API key over HTTP when endpoint is misconfigured
findings.issue: The openai provider sends Authorization: Bearer header with no enforcement that the endpoint uses TLS. If a user configures a remote http:// endpoint with an API key, it is transmitted in cleartext.
findings.impact: API key exposure to network observers if user misconfigures a remote HTTP endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: User sets llm_api.endpoint to http://remote-server:8080 with api_key_env=OPENAI_API_KEY; API key transmitted in cleartext over the network.

remediation.fix: In newOpenAICompatProvider, log a warning or reject if apiKey is set and endpoint scheme is http:// with a non-localhost host
remediation.verify: Add unit test verifying the warning/rejection
remediation.prevent: Document in docs/llm-providers.md that remote endpoints must use HTTPS

findings.title: .gitignore missing common sensitive file patterns
findings.issue: Missing patterns for .env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key, credentials.*, secrets.*. The PD config is stored outside the repo so risk is low.
findings.impact: Accidental commit of sensitive files if created in the repo directory.
findings.failure_scenario: Developer creates a .env file with API keys in the repo directory and accidentally commits it.

remediation.verify: Confirm git check-ignore matches the new patterns

findings.title: math/rand used for identifier generation instead of crypto/rand
findings.issue: Uses math/rand seeded with time.Now().UnixNano() for generating IDs. Used in pkg/pd/dev.go for dev fixture IDs and pkg/tui/approvals.go for approval request IDs. Predictable if process start time is known.
findings.impact: Minimal. Internal TUI identifiers for local state only. No network-facing or authentication use.
findings.failure_scenario: If rand.ID output were ever used as a security token, an attacker knowing process start time could predict all generated IDs.

remediation.fix: Switch to crypto/rand if IDs are ever used in a security-sensitive context
remediation.prevent: Lint rule to flag math/rand imports in non-test files

strengths.detail: Per-arg variable substitution closes prior split-on-spaces vulnerability
shQuote() for proper POSIX shell escaping
deniedFlags list prevents overriding security-critical flags
All GitHub Actions SHA-pinned, workflow-level permissions: read-all, no dangerous triggers, dependabot configured
OpenAI provider excludes response body from error messages to prevent token leakage
All PD API calls use contextWithTimeout() with 30s default
No hardcoded secrets found in entire codebase
All dependencies are well-known org-backed modules; Dependabot configured for gomod and github-actions
